verdict.rationale: Antigravity's own IDE is described by community users as a VSCode fork. Its Editor view documents a context-aware agent and natural-language code commands, and a conversation prompt box with a model selector is documented, so developers can talk to the assistant inside the editor with codebase context. Missing for 10: detailed first-party docs on the in-editor chat panel (e.g., selection/file-context attachment, inline chat behavior) and hands-on corroboration of chat quality inside the IDE.

support.subject: As a developer, I can chat with the coding assistant directly inside my IDE for contextual help

citations.quote: Google Antigravity's Editor view offers tab autocompletion, natural language code commands, and a configurable, and context-aware configurable agent.
Users can select which reasoning model they want to use within the model selector drop-down under the conversation prompt box
it looks to be a VSCode fork very similar to Cursor, with support for Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-OSS 120B models.
